title: AI biodiversity monitoring
summary: SBER describes automated camera-trap analysis for 25 species, aiming to reduce manual image review and improve biodiversity monitoring.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The system combines an object detector with a classifier for 25 native species. The intended workflow removes irrelevant images and supports ecological review. Further species and data modalities are planned. Field-work savings and conservation outcomes remain unquantified.
purpose: Reduce manual review of camera-trap imagery and organize species information.

ratings.reason: A 25-species camera-trap classifier is described without a measured field-workflow improvement.
No population or ecosystem conservation outcome is attributed to the model.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 11: AI biodiversity monitoring

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: AI sorts camera-trap imagery for biodiversity monitoring
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
